declared_proposition: Let F be any finite collection of features of (n,n+2), each periodic with a fixed modulus, and let M be a common period. For every residue a mod M with gcd(a,M)=gcd(a+2,M)=1, there are infinitely many primes p for which F(p,p+2)=F(a,a+2) while p+2 is composite. Choose a prime ell not dividing 2M, impose p=a mod M and p=-2 mod ell, and apply Dirichlet to the resulting reduced CRT class. Therefore no finite periodic fingerprint, even conditioned on p being prime and local admissibility of p+2, can certify twin-prime mass.
mathematical_argument: CRT gives b modulo M ell. Since a is reduced modulo M and -2 is nonzero modulo ell, gcd(b,M ell)=1. Dirichlet's theorem gives infinitely many primes p=b mod M ell. Periodicity gives the same feature vector as a modulo M, while ell divides p+2; for all sufficiently large such primes, p+2 is a proper composite multiple of ell. A finite family of periods is replaced by their lcm.

reproducible_computation.no_go_scope: The theorem does not show that twins are finite. It excludes only fixed finite periodic features as a sufficient certificate. Growing moduli and signed Type II information remain outside it.

logical_limit: No growing-modulus signed Type II lower bound for Lambda(n)Lambda(n+2) is proved.

route_decision.discard: any fixed finite periodic fingerprint, even after conditioning the first entry to be prime, as a twin certificate
route_decision.retain: growing nonperiodic parity-sensitive bilinear information for the actual shift-two Lambda correlation

claim_boundary: No twin-prime proof or counterexample; one exact periodic-feature no-go theorem and five CRT witnesses only.
